title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (pp. ~727–730 of the Longue Marche continuation). S is a connected scheme over Q with geometric point s̄, and π_1 = π_1(S, s̄). A is an abelian group and j : A → G_m(S) a homomorphism into the group of units Γ(S, O_S^*). T = T_∞ = \hat Z(1), the Tate module of roots of unity.

Taking all n-th roots of the units j(a) gives a profinite Kummer extension E_∞(j)_S of A by T: (342) earlier, an extension of A by T. G_j is the group of automorphisms of this extension that act on T through some μ ∈ \hat Z^* and trivially on A. It sits in an exact sequence
1 → Hom_Z(A,T) → G_j → \hat Z^*  (345).
The Galois action gives a 'Kummer representation' ρ_j : π_1 → G_j (346), lifting the cyclotomic character.

This page proves functoriality in A. Given a homomorphism i : A' → A (347), set j' = j∘i (348). The Kummer extension E_∞(j')_S is the pullback of E_∞(j)_S along i. Hence there is a homomorphism G_j → G_{j'}, and it is injective if i is surjective. It fits in the commutative diagram (349):
- on the Hom terms it is the transpose Hom(A,T) → Hom(A',T) of i;
- on \hat Z^* it is the identity;
- it is compatible with ρ_j, ρ_{j'} and the cyclotomic character.

Conclusion (continued on the next page): to study the structure of Im ρ_j, functoriality reduces us to the case j injective (350). One factors j through A/Ker j; for the quotient map, G_{\bar j} → G_j is injective and ρ_j factors through it.

The next page then splits the problem using π_1^+ = Ker(cyclotomic character), giving 1 → Im ρ^+ → Im ρ → Γ → 1. The aim is to measure the 'size' (openness/index) of the image of the Kummer representation, i.e. Kummer theory for G_m over a base of finite type over Q. This is the toric/rank-zero case of Galois images of 1-motives [A → G_m].
errors: 'Injective if i surjective' is correct but only a sufficient condition. Hom(A,T) → Hom(A',T) is injective iff Hom(coker i, \hat Z(1)) = 0, e.g. when coker i is finite or divisible. The reduction to injective j only needs the surjective case, so there is no gap.
Minor: the transcription writes ξ for the map A → G_m(S); in the manuscript the label appears to be j (j' for the composite), consistent with the next page's (350) and G_j.

ideas.what: Profinite Kummer extension of A by \hat Z(1) attached to j : A → G_m(S), with its group G_j and Galois representation π_1 → G_j ⊂ Hom(A,\hat Z(1)) ⋊ \hat Z^*
ideas.modern_name: Kummer representation / ℓ-adic (adelic) realization of the 1-motive [A → G_m]
ideas.usually_credited_to: Kummer theory classical; Bashmakov (1960s–70s), Ribet (1979), Deligne's 1-motives (Hodge III, 1974); later Bertrand, Jossen, Perucca
ideas.where_published: The Kummer class formalism appears in SGA 4/SGA 4½-type contexts and in the Longue Marche; this exact presentation is unsure.

ideas.what: Functoriality of G_j in A via pullback of extensions; reduction to j injective
ideas.modern_name: Contravariant functoriality of Kummer extensions / of the 1-motive realization

ideas.what: Openness of the cyclotomic image for S of finite type over Q (previous page) and the splitting via π_1^+ (next page)
ideas.modern_name: Image of Galois in Kummer theory; open image results (Bashmakov–Ribet)

deep.surprise_reason: A routine functoriality step in a Kummer-theoretic computation, whose content (open-image questions for Kummer representations of G_m) is well covered by Bashmakov–Ribet style results and 1-motive theory. Nothing on this page is new.
transcription_corrections: The homomorphism in (348) is labelled j (not ξ), and the curved composite arrow is labelled j'. Accordingly read E_∞(j')_S, E_∞(j)_S, G_j → G_{j'}, consistent with the next page.

In (349) the lower vertical arrows are labelled γ_{j'} (curved, from π_1 to G_{j'}), γ_j (from π_1 to G_j), and the diagonal from π_1 to \hat Z^* 'car. cyclot.'. The labels are γ, not ρ, matching γ_j on the next page; π_1 appears as π_1 at the bottom.
The crossed-out start '[-Fq-]' is likely an aborted 'G...' or 'Fig'. It is immaterial.
